subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Erik Elliott is a geochemist who studies fluorescent minerals, a class of minerals that emit visible light under specific conditions.
• Photoluminescence, or light emission when exposed to ultraviolet radiation, is a central property of fluorescent minerals.
• Triboluminescence, or light emission when mechanically stressed, is a central property of fluorescent minerals.
• A specimen of sphalerite studied by Elliott exhibits triboluminescence by releasing flashes of orange light when scratched, crushed, or struck sharply.
• Elliott: "These minerals reveal a hidden chemistry of light, one that our eyes cannot detect until the right conditions unlock it."
prompt: The student wants to provide a specific example of triboluminescence in fluorescent minerals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: A specimen of sphalerite studied by geochemist Erik Elliott exhibits triboluminescence by releasing flashes of orange light when scratched, crushed, or struck sharply.
choices.B: The triboluminescence observed in Erik Elliott's fluorescent minerals reveals "a hidden chemistry of light, one that our eyes cannot detect until the right conditions unlock it."
choices.C: Fluorescent minerals, such as the sphalerite studied by Erik Elliott, can exhibit photoluminescence under ultraviolet radiation and triboluminescence under mechanical stress.
choices.D: A specimen of sphalerite studied by Erik Elliott is an example of a fluorescent mineral, a class in which triboluminescence is a central property.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. The sentence effectively provides a specific example of triboluminescence in fluorescent minerals, identifying the sphalerite specimen studied by Erik Elliott and specifying the concrete elements that illustrate the property: flashes of orange light released when the specimen is scratched, crushed, or struck sharply.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect. While the sentence mentions that fluorescent minerals can exhibit triboluminescence under mechanical stress, it offers only a general definition of the property rather than the concrete example — what the sphalerite actually does when stressed — that the question requests.
